abstract: This paper presents updated estimates of long-run fiscal gaps for 35 OECD and accession candidate countries using the OECD Global Long-Term Model. The long-run fiscal gap measures the fiscal adjustment required at the 2060 horizon to keep public debt ratios stable near current levels while maintaining current service standards and benefit entitlements. The methodology incorporates several refinements, including projected increases in defence spending and a more detailed treatment of primary expenditure. In the absence of additional policy action, the median country would require a fiscal adjustment of 4.7 percentage points of GDP between 2027 and 2060 to stabilise debt, with substantially larger adjustments in some countries. Population ageing is the main driver of long-run fiscal pressures through higher pension, health and long-term care spending, compounded in many cases by weak initial fiscal positions. The paper also assesses the sensitivity of fiscal gaps to key assumptions and policy scenarios.
title: Illustrating long-run fiscal challenges using the Long-Term Model

abstract: We estimate the causal effect of big manufacturing plant closures and downsizing on the socioeconomic composition of Canadian cities between 2001 and 2021. Our instrumental variables estimates show that big manufacturing plant closures and downsizing—large local labour demand shocks—lead to less population growth and a shift in the demographic composition of cities toward an older population and less families. We find no other robust sociodemographic changes following big manufacturing plant closures. Exploiting heterogeneity across cities, we also find no robust evidence of city‐level characteristics that mitigate the negative effects of large local labour demand shocks.
title: Deindustrialization and demographic change: Evidence from big plant closures and downsizing

abstract: In recent years, ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) ratings have become critical in guiding investment decisions and fostering corporate green development. However, the growing phenomenon of corporate greenwashing—where companies falsely enhance their environmental credentials—has raised concerns about the accuracy and reliability of ESG ratings. This paper addresses a key gap in the literature by investigating the reputational buffering role of high ESG ratings for greenwashing firms and their impact on corporate green development. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2010 to 2021, we use machine learning to measure corporate green development and construct matched samples to improve comparability between treated and control firms. Our findings show that ESG rating disagreement increases after independently identified greenwashing events, suggesting that greenwashing adds firm-specific information ambiguity to the normal methodological divergence among ESG rating agencies. However, the results further show that high ESG ratings are associated with stronger corporate green development among greenwashing firms, consistent with a reputational buffering mechanism. Moreover, stricter environmental regulations and higher media ESG attention mitigate the rating disagreement, while lenient regulatory environments and lower media ESG attention exacerbate them. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that this reputational buffering effect is more pronounced among firms with a higher proportion of environmentally experienced executives. This study also finds that ESG rating discrepancy negatively moderate the reputational buffer effect of high ESG ratings in corporate greenwashing scenarios. The study makes a significant contribution by highlighting the limitations of the ESG rating system during the research period and calling for stricter regulatory oversight to ensure transparency and accuracy. It also offers a new approach for measuring corporate green development, providing valuable insights for investors, regulators, and corporate managers in addressing greenwashing and refining ESG evaluation systems.

abstract: We introduce the Infinite Period Traveling Salesman Problem ( ∞ -TSP), a generalization of the classical TSP, in which a single service provider repeatedly visits the same set of customers. Our approach leverages the aspiration core, a cooperative game-theoretic concept that extends the classical core to cases where it may be empty, while allowing the formation of proper coalitions. The aspiration core provides robust cost allocation rules and identifies the subsets of customers who should be visited together in specific tours. When the core of the one-shot Traveling Salesman Game is empty, the suggested tour schedule leads to a strictly lower average cost per visit than repeating a single grand tour. We further refine our framework using the aspiration nucleolus, a unique cost allocation selected from the aspiration core.
title: Beyond the grand tour: The aspiration core approach to the Infinite-Period Traveling Salesman Problem

abstract: Auctioning access rights to private providers through competitive tendering has become a central instrument for governments to regulate markets and public services. While efficient in allocating licenses, such auctions may generate monopolistic market structures with adverse effects on consumer welfare. We experimentally evaluate two policy interventions to mitigate these outcomes: introducing post-tender competition and imposing minimum production obligations on winning firms. Our results show that performance obligations substantially improve welfare by raising output and consumer surplus, albeit at the cost of reduced auction revenue. Extending the design with additional treatments, we demonstrate that genuine competition yields even stronger welfare gains. These findings highlight a trade-off between government revenue and consumer welfare in auction design. We conclude that while obligations are an effective tool to counter monopoly distortions, sustaining competition remains essential to maximise total surplus at the market level.
title: Single and Multi-Winner Auctions with Performance Obligation

abstract: We analyse the decline of household saving rates in the bottom half of the income distribution in Germany since the 2000s, which was accompanied by relatively lim- ited increases in consumption inequality compared to income inequality. We com- bine survey data on household consumption with our own survey on consumption visibility and status relevance to test for upwards directed social status compar-isons as an explanation of these trends. We find that non-rich households shift their income allocations towards more visible and status relevant areas of consumption when incomes at the top rise relative to their own. Renter households offset higher status consumption by reducing expenditures on other consumption components. In contrast, homeowners maintain higher status-oriented consumption expenditures, particularly on housing, by considerably reducing their saving rates.
title: Income Inequality, Household Consumption and Status Competition in Germany*

abstract: Motivated by an application at the Raleigh-Durham International Airport, we consider a service system in which a manager aims to track the number of people in the system based only on noisy observations of arrivals and departures over a time horizon. We study two tracking problems in this context. In the busyness tracking problem, the manager seeks to determine whether the system is busy or not, whereas in the population tracking problem, the manager tracks the number of people in the system and accumulates losses as squared errors. We characterize the cumulative losses of various policies in an asymptotic regime in which the time horizon grows large. We prove general lower bounds on the cumulative loss of any policy and propose relatively simple policies that achieve these lower bounds, up to logarithmic terms. These policies outperform naive tracking policies in many instances. Finally, we characterize the impact of having the ability to periodically inspect the system at a cost. We find that effective population tracking policies take opportunities to reset the population count to accurate estimates to stop the accumulation of error. Without inspections, this is achieved by resetting the population count to zero when a near-empty system is detected based on observing the departure stream. Inspections, although coming at a cost, allow for greater flexibility in the timing of corrections and, hence, improved performance. We demonstrate the performance of our policies using real-world data we collected by installing people-counting sensors at the airport. This paper was accepted by Vivek Farias, data science. Funding: Financial support from the Triangle Impact Challenge 2021 is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.05152 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Data-Driven Population Tracking in Service Systems

abstract: Short-form video platforms have become central to debates about digital overuse and sleep disruption, yet causal evidence on their behavioral impacts remains limited. We study the effects of adopting short-form video in the context of TikTok, which pioneered the format and accounts for a large share of global short-form video consumption. Using granular smartphone touchstream data from a large opt-in panel of U.S. Android users, we track app usage, screen time, and inferred sleep behavior before and after TikTok adoption. We employ a difference-in-differences framework leveraging a high-frequency app usage data set from nearly 7,000 TikTok adopters. Our findings reveal a significant increase in overall screen time—averaging 221 minutes per week for heavy TikTok users—following TikTok adoption, alongside notable declines in usage of other social media and gaming apps, suggesting a strong substitution effect. The screen time effects are highest during late night hours. We also observe shifts in sleep patterns, including delayed bedtimes and a moderate reduction in sleep duration, among high-intensity users. We observe no effects for low-intensity users, who engage minimally with TikTok postadoption. Our findings show that short-form video adoption expands total digital attention rather than merely reallocating it, with important implications for platform design, regulation, and digital well-being. As a side result, our analysis provides clear evidence of substitutability between TikTok and traditional social media platforms, which has important implications for competition policy. This paper was accepted by D. J. Wu, information systems. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08260 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Impact of Short-Form Videos on Screentime and Sleep: Evidence from TikTok

abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that plays a key role in regulating global climate, including moderating temperatures in Europe and the North Atlantic. Its potential collapse due to global warming is widely considered one of the more likely climate tipping points. This paper examines the economic implications of such a collapse using a dynamic spatially integrated assessment model (S-IAM) of the world economy. Scandinavia and parts of Russia are predicted to experience significant losses in GDP and welfare, while southern Europe, northern Africa, and Brazil benefit from slightly colder temperatures. S-IAMs generally predict that global warming is especially harmful to low-income regions, but an AMOC collapse could mitigate some of these negative impacts in parts of the developing world while instead harming some of the more advanced economies. This lowers spatial inequality, but global welfare drops by 1.9% by 2200 under an intermediate-emissions scenario.
title: Evaluating the Spatial Consequences of a Climate Tipping Point

abstract: The Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) estimator is widely used for estimating bilateral gravity equations. Its consistency requires only a correctly specified conditional mean. Conventional inference, however, also requires finite-variance scores and Gaussian limits. We show that these conditions fail: bilateral flows are Pareto-tailed, PPML scores have a stable limit under a structural gravity data-generating process, and sandwich confidence intervals are too narrow. We retain PPML for point estimation but replace sandwich inference with an m-out-of-n bootstrap robust to heavy tails. Across three bilateral data settings, the correction is large and overturns conventionally significant gravity coefficients.
title: PPML and Heavy-Tailed Trade and Factor Flows: Why Standard Inference Fails and How to Fix It

abstract: How successful is European integration in removing non-tariff trade barriers? We study how Brexit affected UK firms' input sourcing and sales. The post-Brexit Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) reduced sales and input expenditure at firms with higher pre-Brexit EU trade exposure. It also caused firms to switch towards domestic and non-EU inputs. Through the lens of a trade model, the switch in input sourcing implies the TCA increased trade costs on EU imports by 21% and raised unit production costs by 3.1% for the average UK importer. Our results indicate EU membership secures large reductions in trade costs.

abstract: This paper studies how international firms hedge against trade-cost uncertainty. We analyze two margins of adjustment: foreign market entry (exporting versus foreign investment) and invoicing in free-on-board (FOB) or cost-insurance-freight-inclusive (CIF) prices. Under oligopolistic competition and price rigidity, trade-cost volatility jointly shapes entry and invoicing choices. Firms with small market shares prefer exporting and FOB-price invoicing, while firms with large market shares favor foreign investment and CIF-price invoicing. Using a novel measure of trade-cost volatility constructed from French customs data, we provide empirical support for these mechanisms and document the joint determination of entry and invoicing decisions. Counterfactual analyses based on the structurally estimated and calibrated model indicate that trade-cost uncertainty has sizable effects on these decisions.

abstract: Il est difficile d’imaginer atteindre la neutralité carbone d’ici 2050, comme le prévoit l’Accord de Paris, sans une taxe carbone. Cet article estime que pour atteindre cet objectif par le biais d’une taxe carbone, il faudra une trajectoire fiscale culminant à environ 1 300 dollars par tonne de CO₂, soit dix fois les prix actuels pratiqués partout dans le monde, et souligne à quel point les coûts de transition seront répartis de manière très inégale entre les différents secteurs. Le principe intuitif de la « cheminée », selon lequel les plus gros émetteurs directs devraient payer le plus, s'avère erroné : les coûts sont en réalité prédits par une simple statistique mesurant le degré d'exposition d'un secteur à travers sa chaîne d'approvisionnement.
authors: Eric Jondeau, Côme Poirier, Gauthier Vermandel
title: L'illusion de la cheminée : qui paie réellement pour la neutralité carbone ?

abstract: Monetary policy invariably leaves a fiscal footprint; not only whether but also when that footprint is eliminated is central to monetary transmission. We provide closed-form solutions for a New Keynesian model with government debt. Debt provides liquidity services. Debt, thus, affects the natural rate of interest. We show how the timing of fiscal adjustment shapes the effects of monetary tightening. As adjustment is deferred, outcomes become reminiscent of active fiscal policy, even if fiscal policy is known eventually to absorb the footprint: Even with finite fiscal delays, a rate hike can become inflationary, and potentially expansionary. The effect is found in data and quantitatively also in a richer quantitative HANK-OLG.
title: Fiscal Constraints on Monetary Policy: How Debt Limits Monetary Effectiveness

abstract: Artificial intelligence may augment workers, displace labor, or do both. We elicit beliefs from more than 64,000 adults across 32 countries, covering 65% of the world's population and 85% of global output. Workers are substantially more likely to expect artificial intelligence to facilitate than threaten their jobs. Facilitation is more prevalent in lower-productivity countries, whereas threat is unrelated to productivity. Facilitation and threat often coexist within individuals, indicating that perceived benefits and risks are distinct rather than opposite dimensions. They are also associated with different macroeconomic expectations: facilitation with stronger expected growth and employment, and threat with weaker employment and higher inflation. These heterogeneous beliefs may shape the diffusion and acceptance of artificial intelligence across countries.
title: Will AI Help or Hurt Work and the Economy? What People Around the World Expect

abstract: Non-fundamental inflows into the stock market loosen financial conditions and raise output, while the policy rate responds gradually. Such financial noise explains up to 20% of the variance of financial conditions and output. These facts motivate a macroeconomic model with noise traders, risk-averse arbitrageurs, and gradual interest rate adjustment. In this model, Financial Conditions Index (FCI) targeting can improve macroeconomic stabilization: the central bank announces its expected FCI as a soft near-term target and adjusts the policy rate to keep conditions near it. This commitment reduces FCI volatility, thereby "recruiting" arbitrageurs to insulate the FCI and aggregate demand from noise.
title: Financial Conditions Targeting

abstract: We study monetary policy transmission to innovation using a representative survey of German firms. Firms report persistent innovation investment reductions averaging 20% due to the ECB’s 2022–23 monetary tightening. A survey-based experiment shows that rate hikes lower and cuts raise innovation investment, with state-dependent asymmetry reflecting exit from innovation activity at high policy rates. Forward guidance stimulates innovation investment by resolving policy-rate uncertainty, providing novel evidence of its medium-term, supply-side effects. We document two distinct transmission channels—financing and demand expectations—with amplification under simultaneous exposure. Our findings suggest that monetary policy affects innovation-driven technological progress typically considered longer-term and policy-exogenous.
title: Beyond the Short Run: Monetary Policy and Innovation Investment

abstract: We study how the shale revolution and the U.S. transition from petroleum importer to net exporter have changed the macroeconomic effects of oil shocks. Using oil supply news shocks identified from OPEC announcements, a time-varying model of the U.S. macroeconomy shows that the contractionary effects weakened over time and eventually became expansionary. State-dependent local projections link this change to the U.S. petroleum trade balance. The improvement goes beyond mechanical net export effects: as the terms-of-trade response turns more favorable, consumption, equity valuations, and activity strengthen broadly across sectors and regions, pointing to general-equilibrium income and wealth effects. A counterfactual analysis of the 2022 oil price surge implies sharply different paths for U.S. activity, prices, and monetary policy under the propagation mechanisms prevailing before the shale boom vs. the early 2020s.

abstract: Urban climate policies are increasingly expected not only to reduce carbon emissions but also to reorganize the collaborative networks through which green innovation is generated. While existing studies show that China’s Low-Carbon City Pilot (LCCP) policy increases green innovation output, little is known about whether and how it reshapes the structure of innovation collaboration across and within cities. Drawing on the extended Porter Hypothesis, this study examines the impact of the LCCP on green innovation collaboration by focusing on inter-city embeddedness and intra-city complexity. Using a balanced panel of 250 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2006 to 2022, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences approach and construct patent-based indicators to capture cross-city collaborative integration and within-city technological diversity. The results show that the LCCP significantly increases both inter-city embeddedness and intra-city complexity. Digitalization and environmental regulation intensity positively moderate these effects, and the joint implementation of the Innovation City Pilot (ICP) and the LCCP generates strong complementary impacts. The effects are more pronounced in eastern and large cities, key environmental protection cities, and directly designated pilot cities, but are weaker in resource-based regions. These findings suggest that policymakers should integrate low-carbon city policies with innovation-oriented pilot programs, strengthen digital infrastructure that supports cross-city knowledge collaboration, and provide targeted institutional support for resource-based and less-developed cities to avoid uneven policy effects. This study contributes to the literature by moving beyond innovation quantity to examine how environmental regulation reshapes innovation collaboration networks, providing new evidence on the collaborative mechanisms through which low-carbon policies foster green technological upgrading.

abstract: Green credit can finance both abatement and output expansion, so its emissions effect is ambiguous for financially constrained firms. We develop an energy-finance model in which banks post project-contingent terms before a firm selects a verifiable production–abatement plan and carbon prices are realized. The main model separates verified abatement from positive carbon collateral. Green credit lowers emissions only when the technique effect dominates the scale effect. Competitive break-even pricing transmits carbon-price risk to loan rates without distorting risk-neutral operations, whereas lender market power can convert the same risk into lower abatement and higher emissions intensity. Paid allowance allocation acts as a policy-induced financing friction: competitive credit absorbs the upfront cost, while concentrated lending can amplify the debt burden and generate adverse emission responses. A transition-finance extension shows that carbon-deficit borrowers face a reversed default tail and may be harmed by carbon-price support. Additional contract extensions indicate that performance-linked pricing and use-of-proceeds restrictions improve environmental outcomes only when incentives are genuine and funds are not highly fungible. Carbon policy, banking structure, and loan design therefore jointly determine whether green finance produces real decarbonization.
title: Green credit under carbon price risk: financing frictions, banking market power, and firm emissions

abstract: Previous studies have examined the anomaly of a sudden increase in corporate investment in the fourth quarter and explained the tax planning logic behind this unusual investment phenomenon. With the application of information technologies such as big data and cloud computing in the field of tax enforcement, the space for tax evasion has been greatly narrowed. However, existing literature has not yet provided a clear answer to whether and how digital tax enforcement affects corporate abnormal investment behaviors. To fill this research gap, this study takes the Golden Tax Phase III Project as a quasi-natural experiment and adopts the difference-in-differences (DID) method to empirically test the causal relationship between digital tax enforcement and corporate abnormal investment. The empirical results show that digital tax enforcement significantly exacerbates corporate abnormal investment. Mechanism tests reveal that digital tax enforcement significantly inhibits tax evasion by firms, forcing them to shift from tax evasion to tax planning, which in turn highlights the tax shield value and tax planning function of year-end investment. Meanwhile, the exacerbating effect of digital tax enforcement on corporate abnormal investment is more pronounced for firms with heavier tax burdens, higher capital intensity, and weaker cost-shifting ability. This study has important theoretical and practical implications for optimizing tax system reforms to promote effective corporate investment.

abstract: This study examines how the stance of monetary policy shapes the effectiveness of macroprudential tools in mitigating systemic risk. While prior literature highlights the stabilizing role of macroprudential policy, evidence on its interaction with monetary policy is mixed and often neglects differences across instruments. We address this gap by constructing separate indices for tools targeting bank capital and liquidity versus those aimed at borrowers, using a panel of 37 countries (2011–2021) and employing panel fixed-effects and system-GMM estimations. Our results show that only tools targeting bank capital and liquidity significantly reduce systemic risk, measured via an aggregate country-level banks’ Z-score. Importantly, their effectiveness is substantially weakened under a restrictive monetary stance, revealing a critical policy interaction transmitted through bank profitability. These findings highlight the need to consider the prevailing monetary environment when designing macroprudential interventions.
title: Policy interactions and systemic stability: How monetary conditions influence macroprudential effectiveness?

abstract: This paper explores the interplay between female representation in mutual funds’ management teams and their voting behavior. We find that women-led mutual funds are more likely to support environmental and social (ES) proposals, but not governance ones. This result is robust to excluding sustainable funds, alleviating concerns that the findings are driven by the self-selection of female fund managers into sustainable funds. While women-led mutual funds are also more likely to vote with management in firms headed by female CEOs, this does not conflict with their greater support for ES shareholder proposals. Overall, our results suggest that female representation in fund management teams is related to their voting behavior on ES issues.
title: The voting behavior of women-led mutual funds

abstract: We measure flow diversification in mutual funds using the cross-sectional correlation of daily flows across investor clienteles. Greater flow diversification is associated with lower future flow volatility, smaller subsequent outflows, and lower cash holdings. We decompose flow correlation into predictable and unexpected components. Unexpectedly low flow correlation is associated with higher post-outflow fund returns, mitigating outflow-induced externalities on incumbent shareholders. Flow diversification also dampens the higher flow-performance sensitivity of illiquid funds, partially offsetting strategic complementarities that can generate fragility.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Flow Diversification

abstract: I study the environmental impacts of agricultural input subsidy reform by evaluating Zambia’s staggered transition from a traditional physical fertilizer distribution program to a flexible electronic voucher system. Using a 5 km 5 km spatial panel of satellite-derived water quality measures and a staggered difference-in-differences design, I estimate the downstream environmental effects of the reform from 2010 to 2023. I find that the introduction of the e-voucher significantly improves downstream water quality, reducing chlorophyll-a concentration by 13.0%, phycocyanin concentration by 11.0%, and total suspended matter by 7.5%. The estimated effects are larger in districts with higher densities of private agro-dealers and are concentrated in areas with highly leachable soils and historically intensive maize monocropping. At the household level, I find that greater input flexibility reduces synthetic nitrogen use and increases crop diversification toward nitrogen-fixing legumes. These changes are consistent with a reduction in nutrient losses and improvements in soil stability. Overall, the findings suggest that replacing fixed agricultural subsidies with flexible systems can improve downstream water quality while encouraging more sustainable agricultural practices.
journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management

title: Agricultural input subsidy reform and water quality: Evidence from Zambia

abstract: We investigate whether in-kind food aid can generate larger nutritional gains through the strategic allocation of different food boxes across households. Using data from a randomized evaluation of a nationwide food aid program in Egypt, we compare a staple-heavy food box with a more expensive nutrition-sensitive food box. We apply machine learning methods to estimate household-level heterogeneity in treatment effects and use these estimates to evaluate allocation rules under budget constraints. We find substantial heterogeneity in impacts on calorie intake, food insecurity experience, and dietary diversity. Observable household characteristics predict this heterogeneity, but the relevant predictors differ across outcomes and food box types. Predicted impacts align closely with baseline deprivation for calorie intake and dietary diversity, but less so for food insecurity experience, particularly under the staple box. Thus, trade-offs between targeting the most deprived and the most impacted households are limited. Instead, the more salient challenge is prioritizing among competing nutritional objectives. Using a multi-armed Qini curve that accounts explicitly for program costs, we show that, under a fixed budget, the estimated optimal policy assigns the nutrition-sensitive food box to most treated households despite its higher cost. The gains from covariate-based allocation are strongest for food insecurity experience and more limited for the other outcomes. Overall, our findings highlight the potential of ML-informed targeting in food aid programs, while also showing that targeting priorities depend on the nutritional objective being pursued.
title: Machine learning and heterogeneity in food aid impacts: Foundations for improved targeting

abstract: We examine how cultural norms shape attitudes toward immigration. Using representative survey data on German university students from the 1990s, we exploit the stark cultural differences between former East and West Germany to study whether moving to a different cultural environment impacts these attitudes. We address the endogeneity of the decision to move by comparing students who moved across the East-West border with those who moved within the former East Germany. We also exploit plausibly exogenous variation in exposure arising from the national allocation mechanism used to place students at universities. Students who moved from the former East to the former West Germany are around 7 percentage points less likely to strongly support limiting immigration than students who moved within the former East Germany.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: How cultural norms affect attitudes toward immigration

abstract: In a three-stage global public good coalition formation game, Kornek and Edenhofer (2020) propose a transfer scheme in the spirit of mechanism design which allows to stabilize large coalitions, including the grand coalition. The transfer scheme addresses the free-rider problem in terms of participation. In order to address the free-rider problem in terms of compliance with transfer obligations, they propose a deposit-refund scheme in the spirit of Gerber and Wichardt (2009) and others. However, McEvoy and McGinty (2023) argue in a comment that the compliance issue has not yet been solved because signatories would have neither an incentive to pay the deposit nor the transfer. In this paper, we show how to modify the original proposal in KE (2020) to render compliance an equilibrium choice. We also demonstrate that the transfer scheme retains its desirable properties when considering asymmetric countries. It emerges that it is promising to generalize further the setting of Kornek and Edenhofer (2020).
title: A Mechanism for Addressing Participation and Compliance for the Provision of Global Public Goods

abstract: Many colleges permit course retakes, yet their effects on academic success remain largely unknown. We study a four-year university that canceled a grade-replacement policy in 1995 and reinstated it in 2001. Exploiting these policy shifts and the disproportionate retaking response among D/F students relative to C students, we estimate the causal effects of retaking using an instrumental-variables design. Grade replacement substantially increased retaking among students who initially earned D/F grades. We find broadly robust evidence that retaking improves same-subject persistence and subsequent performance among students who continue in the subject. Estimates for university-level retention and four-year graduation are less robust, ranging from positive to no detectable effects. Overall, grade replacement encourages struggling students to retake courses without harming their short- or longer-run academic progress.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: Retaking to succeed: Causal evidence on optional course retaking in college

abstract: Human decision making in the newsvendor paradigm systematically deviates from the predictions of expected profit maximization, yet the cognitive mechanisms underlying these deviations remain contested. We investigate whether these biases arise from distorted utility evaluation or from adaptive learning induced by repeated feedback. Across three laboratory experiments ( N = 214 ), we compare behavior under decision from description, decision from experience, and newsvendor environments while varying information availability. The first experiment combines behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) data, the second replicates the behavioral findings without EEG, and the third extends the analysis to a multi-alternative setting with continuous demand. We document two robust patterns in newsvendor environments: decision accuracy inferior to random guessing, and positive correlation between choice and realized demand. These patterns are absent in one-shot descriptive decisions and cannot be explained by standard utility-based models. Neural evidence shows that repeated environments engage parietal and frontal activity associated with choice deliberation and feedback-based learning, and that memory encoding differs systematically across demand outcomes. Motivated by these findings, we develop a model incorporating probability matching and asymmetric belief updating, which provides a substantially improved fit to observed choices. Our results demonstrate that repeated feedback fundamentally alters the mechanism of economic decision making, highlighting the central role of learning and belief dynamics in generating newsvendor biases.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: Learning and probability matching in newsvendor decisions

abstract: This article partially identifies population treatment effects in observational data under both non‐random treatment assignment and sample selection. Bounds are provided for both average and quantile population treatment effects, combining assumptions for the selected and the non‐selected subsamples. We show how different assumptions help narrow identification regions, and we illustrate our methods by partially identifying the effect of maternal education on the 2015 PISA math test scores in Brazil. We find that while sample selection considerably increases the uncertainty around the effect of maternal education, it is still possible to calculate informative identification regions.
abstract_zh: 本文在非随机处理分配和样本选择的观察数据中部分识别了总体处理效应。我们为平均和分位数总体处理效应提供了边界，并结合了对被选和非被选子样本的假设。我们展示了不同假设如何有助于缩小识别区域，并通过部分识别母亲教育对巴西2015年PISA数学测试成绩的影响来说明我们的方法。我们发现，尽管样本选择大幅增加了母亲教育效应周围的不确定性，仍然有可能计算出有信息量的识别区域。

abstract: Index insurance is promoted for climate risk management, but basis risk limits scalability. This article develops an ex ante, multi-hazard weather-yield index framework for corn in Paraná, Brazil, tailored to the state’s dual-season system (Safra and Safrinha) and the distinct priorities of farmers and insurers. We combine municipality-level yield panels with climate extreme indicators spanning temperature, precipitation, humidity, radiation, wind, and evaporative demand, and evaluate mean- and tail-focused econometric specifications alongside penalised alternatives to guard against overfitting. Basis risk is treated as two-sided and designable by explicitly trading off false negatives (uncompensated losses) and false positives (unnecessary payouts) through a stakeholder-weighted objective, implemented within clustered municipal zones and season-specific windows. Our framework delivers a transparent mapping from alternative basis risk priorities to contract design choices, offering a practical blueprint for piloting credible index insurance where products are not yet established.
abstract_zh: 指数保险被推广用于气候风险管理，但基差风险限制了其可扩展性。本文为巴西巴拉那州的玉米开发了一个事前、多灾害天气—产量指数框架，该框架针对该州的双季种植体系（Safra和Safrinha）以及农户与保险公司各自不同的优先事项而设计。我们将市级产量面板数据与涵盖温度、降水、湿度、辐射、风和蒸发需求的极端气候指标相结合，并评估以均值和尾部为重点的计量经济学设定以及惩罚性替代方案，以防止过拟合。基差风险被视为双向且可设计的，通过利益相关者加权目标函数，在聚类市政区域和特定季节窗口内，明确权衡假阴性（未获补偿的损失）与假阳性（不必要的赔付）。我们的框架提供了从替代性基差风险优先事项到合同设计选择的透明映射，为在尚未建立相关产品的地区试点可信的指数保险提供了实用蓝图。
title: Seasonal index-based corn insurance design for Brazil: Insights from Safra and Safrinha
title_zh: 基于季节指数的巴西玉米保险设计：来自Safra和Safrinha的启示

abstract: The global energy transition is accelerating battery production, creating policy challenges for countries seeking to join low-carbon supply chains. Research on industrial upgrading and global value chains explains integration into production networks. In contrast, research on the development of green industrial paths establishes the importance of regional preconditions, asset modification, and firm- and system-level agency. Less is known, however, about how system-level actors coordinate these elements in structurally constrained and globally interdependent contexts. This paper examines Morocco's EV battery industry and identifies a mechanism and a boundary condition. Drawing on interviews, policy documents, corporate disclosures and secondary data, it identifies policy-mediated cross-path asset alignment: system-level actors translate external regulatory and market pressures into domestic interventions connecting automotive, logistics, mineral-processing and renewable-energy assets with non-local technology and capital. The resulting pathway combines the renewal of phosphate- and cobalt-related activities with diversification into battery-material production and the prospective importation of cell manufacturing. Although this alignment reduces input, logistics, compliance and market-access constraints and may elicit investment commitments, uneven implementation shows that such commitments do not necessarily produce operational capacity, domestic linkages, capability formation, or durable regional value capture. For energy policy, the findings demonstrate both the importance and limits of coordinating industrial, energy and resource policies under external dependence.
abstract_zh: 全球能源转型正在加速电池生产，为寻求加入低碳供应链的国家带来了政策挑战。关于产业升级和全球价值链的研究解释了如何融入生产网络。相比之下，关于绿色产业路径发展的研究确立了区域先决条件、资产改造以及企业和系统层面能动性的重要性。然而，对于系统层面行为主体如何在结构性受限且全球相互依存的背景下协调这些要素，人们知之甚少。本文考察摩洛哥的电动汽车电池产业，并识别出一种机制和一个边界条件。基于访谈、政策文件、企业披露和二手数据，本文识别出政策中介的跨路径资产对齐：系统层面行为主体将外部监管和市场压力转化为国内干预措施，将汽车、物流、矿产加工和可再生能源资产与非本地技术和资本连接起来。由此形成的路径将磷酸盐和钴相关活动的更新与向电池材料生产的多元化以及未来电芯制造进口结合起来。尽管这种对齐减少了投入、物流、合规和市场准入方面的约束，并可能引发投资承诺，但不均衡的实施表明，此类承诺并不必然产生运营能力、国内联系、能力形成或持久的区域价值捕获。对于能源政策而言，研究结果既表明了在外依赖下协调产业、能源和资源政策的重要性，也表明了其局限性。
title: Battery industrialisation and the energy transition: Policy coordination and industrial path in Morocco
title_zh: 电池工业化与能源转型：摩洛哥的政策协调与产业路径

abstract: Star scientists can have significant impacts on their institutions both through their own productivity and through spillover effects on their co-located colleagues. For newly recruited stars, previous research has shown evidence of positive productivity effects on incumbent scientists in the institutions they join. This paper complements this research by using the same data source to examine the effects of a star’s move on their own research performance in three small open economies (SOEs) - Ireland, Denmark, and New Zealand. We estimate the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) using an event-study difference-in-differences design that compares star movers with non-mover stars who exhibit parallel pre-move productivity trends. Analysing the quality-adjusted productivity of 161-star scientists, we find that moving to a new institution substantially reduces their productivity in the year of the move by 58%, and this effect persists in subsequent years, with an estimated reduction of 42% after four years. One explanation consistent with this combination of negative own-productivity effects and positive peer-spillover effects is that the arriving stars prioritise institution-building activities at their new institution rather than their own research output.
abstract_zh: 明星科学家对其所在机构能够产生显著影响，这种影响既来自其自身生产力，也来自对同址同事的溢出效应。对于新招募的明星科学家，已有研究表明，他们对其加入机构中的在职科学家产生了正向生产力效应。本文利用同一数据来源对这一研究进行补充，考察明星科学家流动对其自身研究表现的影响，研究覆盖三个小型开放经济体（SOEs）——爱尔兰、丹麦和新西兰。我们采用事件研究双重差分设计，将明星流动者与具有平行流动前生产力趋势的非流动明星进行比较，估计处理组平均处理效应（ATT）。通过分析161位明星科学家的质量调整生产力，我们发现，迁至新机构使其在流动当年的生产力大幅下降58%，且这一效应在随后年份持续存在，四年后估计降幅为42%。一种与自身生产力负效应和同行溢出正效应这一组合相符的解释是，新加入的明星科学家优先投入新机构的机构建设活动，而非自身研究产出。
title: Estimating the impact of a star scientist move on their own research productivity
title_zh: 评估明星科学家流动对其自身科研生产力的影响

abstract: In two-sided matching markets without outside options, we compare mechanisms in terms of the number of agents who can manipulate them. Despite the existence of several stable mechanisms that are strategy-proof for one side of the market, we show that there is only one such mechanism that stable-minimizes manipulation: the deferred acceptance mechanism with the short side making proposals. Surprisingly, the Boston mechanism may have fewer manipulators than any stable mechanism. We adapt our main results to markets where only one side has outside options and to many-to-one markets without outside options.
abstract_zh: 在不存在外部选项的双边匹配市场中，我们从能够操纵机制的代理人数量角度对机制进行比较。尽管存在若干对市场一方而言是策略防伪的稳定机制，我们证明，只有一个这样的机制能在稳定机制中最小化操纵：由短边提出申请的延迟接受机制。令人惊讶的是，波士顿机制可能比任何稳定机制拥有更少的操纵者。我们将主要结果推广到仅有一方拥有外部选项的市场，以及不存在外部选项的多对一市场。
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Minimizing manipulation in matching markets without outside options
title_zh: 在无外部选项的匹配市场中最小化操纵

abstract: This paper investigates the heterogeneous transmission of global supply chain disruptions, trade policy uncertainty, tariffs and monetary policy shocks to United States sectoral wages from March 2007 to June 2025. Estimating a Bayesian structural vector autoregression model for major economic sectors, we quantify the dynamic wage responses and calculate the forecast error variance decompositions to identify the primary drivers of wage volatility. The empirical estimates document substantial sectoral heterogeneity. Global supply chain disruptions create significant inflationary pressures on wages, heavily concentrated within service and logistics industries. In contrast, trade policy uncertainty acts as a broad deflationary force across the labour market. Tariff implementations generate sharply divided outcomes between protected and exposed sectors. Additionally, contractionary monetary policy has its most severe dampening effects on wages in interest‐rate‐sensitive, goods‐producing industries. By jointly evaluating these structural shocks at a detailed level, this study demonstrates that aggregate macroeconomic analyses hide critical labour market dynamics, providing highly specific estimates of the distinct forces dictating sectoral wage growth.
abstract_zh: 本文考察了2007年3月至2025年6月期间，全球供应链中断、贸易政策不确定性、关税和货币政策冲击对美国部门工资的异质性传导。通过对主要经济部门估计贝叶斯结构向量自回归模型，我们量化了工资的动态响应，并计算预测误差方差分解，以识别工资波动的主要驱动因素。实证估计记录了显著的部门异质性。全球供应链中断对工资造成显著的通胀压力，且高度集中于服务业和物流业。相比之下，贸易政策不确定性在整个劳动力市场中起到广泛的通缩作用。关税实施在受保护部门与暴露部门之间产生了尖锐分化的结果。此外，紧缩性货币政策对利率敏感型商品生产部门的工资具有最严重的抑制效应。通过在细致层面上联合评估这些结构性冲击，本研究表明，总体宏观经济分析掩盖了关键的劳动力市场动态，并提供了对决定部门工资增长的各股不同力量的高度具体估计。
title: Global Supply Chains and Policy Shocks: Implications for Sectoral Wages
title_zh: 全球供应链与政策冲击：对行业工资的影响

abstract: This paper develops a novel empirical framework to estimate exploitation rates (the ratios of unpaid to paid labor time) and tests the hypothesis that globalization fosters their convergence. By integrating the Leontief input–output model with the New Interpretation of Marxian value theory, the analysis distinguishes between value production and value realization, exploring their distinct implications for global exploitation. Drawing on the GLORIA dataset, comprising 1.2 terabytes of input–output data covering 120 sectors across 164 regions from 1990 to 2023, this study offers the most comprehensive empirical investigation of exploitation rates to date. The analysis spans four levels of aggregation (global, national, sectoral, and country–sectoral) and incorporates alternative classifications of productive and unproductive activities. A key methodological innovation is the comparative estimation of exploitation rates before and after the cross-border and cross-sectoral reallocation of value-added. The findings reveal a global fall in exploitation rates accompanied by absolute convergence. Yet this coexists with relative divergence, sustaining a core–periphery structure within global value chains. While most value is produced in peripheral regions, value realization is concentrated in the core. Unequal exchange, manifested through value transfers from high- to low-exploitation activities, conceals the global hierarchy of labor. By focusing solely on realized value, the System of National Accounts obscures these transfers, attributing peripheral value creation to core economies. The data further highlight the growing relevance of the core–periphery divide across industries. The paper reflects on the implications of these dynamics for theories of uneven development.
abstract_zh: 本文构建了一个新颖的实证框架，用以估算剥削率（即无酬劳动时间与有酬劳动时间之比），并检验全球化促进剥削率趋同这一假说。通过将列昂惕夫投入产出模型与马克思价值理论的新解释相结合，该分析区分了价值生产与价值实现，并探讨二者对全球剥削的不同含义。本研究依托GLORIA数据集，该数据集包含1.2太字节的投入产出数据，覆盖1990年至2023年间164个地区的120个部门，构成了迄今为止对剥削率最为全面的实证考察。分析涵盖四个加总层次（全球、国家、部门以及国家—部门），并纳入生产性与非生产性活动的替代性分类。一个关键的方法论创新在于，对增加值在跨境和跨部门再配置前后的剥削率进行比较估算。研究发现，全球剥削率下降，并伴随绝对趋同。然而，这与相对分化并存，从而在全球价值链内部维持了核心—外围结构。尽管大部分价值在外围地区生产，价值实现却集中于核心地区。表现为价值从高剥削活动向低剥削活动转移的不平等交换，掩盖了劳动的全球等级结构。国民账户体系仅关注已实现价值，因而遮蔽了这些转移，并将外围的价值创造归因于核心经济体。数据进一步凸显了核心—外围分野在各行业间日益增长的重要性。本文反思了这些动态对不平衡发展理论的含义。
title: Measuring global exploitation, 1990–2023: does globalization equalize exploitation rates?
title_zh: 衡量全球剥削，1990–2023：全球化是否使剥削率均等化？

abstract: Economic abuse has recently gained recognition as a distinct form of intimate partner violence in sub-Saharan Africa, with women disproportionately affected. However, limited research has explored its consequences, particularly its impact on food insecurity among women living with HIV, who face compounded vulnerabilities due to stigma, poverty, and health challenges. This study addressed this gap by conducting 39 in-depth interviews with women living with HIV in Ghana who had experienced economic abuse, to understand how this abuse influenced their experiences of food insecurity. Using inductive thematic analysis, we identified critical connections between economic abuse and food insecurity. Participants shared narratives of financial withholding, income sabotage, and coercive control that prevented them from meeting their food needs and those of their children. Many described experiences of self-sacrifice, hunger, and dependence on kinship or religious networks as coping mechanisms. Addressing economic abuse requires stronger legal protections, increased public awareness, and tailored support for women living with HIV.
abstract_zh: 经济虐待近年来在撒哈拉以南非洲被认定为亲密伴侣暴力的一种独特形式，女性受影响尤为严重。然而，探讨其后果的研究仍然有限，尤其是其对感染HIV女性粮食不安全状况的影响，而这一群体因污名、贫困和健康挑战而面临多重脆弱性。本研究通过深度访谈加纳39名曾遭受经济虐待的感染HIV女性，以理解这种虐待如何影响她们的粮食不安全经历，从而填补了这一空白。运用归纳性主题分析，我们识别出经济虐待与粮食不安全之间的关键联系。参与者讲述了经济扣留、收入破坏和强制性控制的经历，这些行为使她们无法满足自身及子女的食物需求。许多人描述了自我牺牲、饥饿以及依赖亲属或宗教网络作为应对机制的经历。解决经济虐待问题需要更有力的法律保护、更高的公众意识以及针对感染HIV女性的定制化支持。
title: Economic abuse and food insecurity among women living with HIV in Ghana
title_zh: 加纳HIV感染女性中的经济虐待与粮食不安全

abstract: The EU’s far-reaching response to a series of major shocks has turned it into a major borrower on international financial markets. Debt issued by the EU on behalf of its member states now stands at close to 5½% of GDP, almost twice as much as six years ago. This column highlights two crucial issues associated with this trend. It reviews implications for conventional debt statistics and looks at debt servicing obligations.
abstract_zh: 欧盟对一系列重大冲击的深远应对，已使其成为国际金融市场上的主要借款方。欧盟代表其成员国发行的债务目前接近GDP的5.5%，几乎是六年前的两倍。本专栏着重探讨与这一趋势相关的两个关键问题：审视其对传统债务统计的影响，并考察债务偿付义务。
title: Lifting the curtain on the EU’s debt

abstract: Geopolitical tensions are increasingly reshaping the flow of trade, investment and capital flows. This column documents that the same process is also reshaping bank lending. Using confidential supervisory data on thousands of international bank lending relationships, the authors show that banks systematically curtail lending to firms exposed to geopolitical risk. The effects are strongest when risks are linked to sanctions and when lending crosses geopolitical blocs, suggesting that geopolitics is a key determinant not only of how much banks lend but also of where they lend – even to their largest clients.
abstract_zh: 地缘政治紧张局势正日益重塑贸易、投资和资本流动的格局。本专栏指出，同一进程也在重塑银行信贷。作者利用涵盖数千个国际银行信贷关系的保密监管数据表明，银行会系统性地削减对暴露于地缘政治风险企业的贷款。当风险与制裁相关、且贷款跨越地缘政治集团时，这种效应最为显著，这表明地缘政治不仅是决定银行放贷规模、也是决定其放贷去向的关键因素——即便对最大客户也是如此。
authors: Dennis Reinhardt, Rhiannon Sowerbutts, Julian Reynolds
title: Geopolitical risk is reshaping global finance, one bank loan at a time
title_zh: 地缘政治风险正通过一笔笔银行贷款重塑全球金融格局

abstract: Professional judgement comes from learning by doing, but AI has the potential to disrupt this learning process. This column explores how randomised access to an AI patent-writing product affects the performance of lawyers on certain writing tasks. Using the AI tool raised the quality of the drafts and compressed performance differentials, especially among junior lawyers. However, on a subsequent task without AI tools, expertise gains from the previous AI use appeared only among senior lawyers with seasoned judgement.
abstract_zh: 专业判断源于干中学，但人工智能有可能扰乱这一学习过程。本专栏探讨随机获取一款AI专利撰写产品如何影响律师在特定写作任务中的表现。使用该AI工具提高了草稿质量并缩小了绩效差异，尤其是在初级律师中。然而，在随后一项不使用AI工具的任务中，此前使用AI所带来的专业能力提升仅出现在具有成熟判断力的资深律师身上。
authors: Tanya Rodchenko, Josh Martin, Zanna Iscenko, Scott Strand, David Pearl, Melissa Ferere, David Autor
title: Better work, not always better workers
title_zh: 更好的工作，而非总是更好的工作者

abstract: This paper analyses how China’s rapid expansion has affected growth in other developing economies through the trade channel. The empirical strategy is a shift-share design that exploits pre-determined variation across countries in the exposure of their exports to China’s import demand and export supply in global markets, well before China became a dominant trader. The paper shows that China’s rising demand for commodities and intermediate goods has had a favorable impact on other developing countries’ growth, while intensified competition from its manufacturing exports has had an adverse effect. The former effect is stronger and therefore the net effect has been positive for most countries. The positive impact is, however, becoming weaker as China’s growth slows down, and developing countries’ longer term growth may also be influenced by the changes in their economic structures induced by China’s trade expansion.

abstract: Three key developments, protectionism, aging, and automation, are affecting the global pattern of industrial production and trade. While these trends affect many countries, they are especially consequential for China, which currently dominates global manufacturing. Using a multi-country model fitted with global trade and robotization data, this paper shows that automation can mitigate the adverse effects of protection and aging on competitiveness, particularly in sectors with a high share of automatable tasks. The impact of a 10 percent decline in labor force in China would be offset by doubling of robot productivity in vehicles, but robot productivity would need to more than triple in computers.

abstract: China’s export performance is characterized by two striking features: a steady rise in export sophistication and the continued prominence of less sophisticated products. In this paper we propose the “Many Chinas” hypothesis, that China’s provinces differ in their comparative advantage, and in how this comparative advantage has evolved over time. Using detailed Chinese customs export data from 1995 to 2023, we investigate the provincial underpinnings of China’s export performance. Three main findings emerge. First, export similarity between Chinese provinces and the advanced economies increased over time, initially more rapidly in the Eastern provinces. Second, despite this increased export similarity with the advanced countries, there remained significant heterogeneity across provinces in 2023. In their export structure, provinces such as Shanghai and Jiangsu resemble most closely the Republic of Korea while Guangdong and Shanxi resemble Viet Nam and the Philippines, respectively. Third, this paper identifies a novel pattern: during the first decade after China’s WTO accession in 2001, the export sophistication of Eastern provinces increased much faster than that of other provinces, but after about 2010, there has been remarkable convergence in sophistication across all provinces.

abstract: We consider official and alternative data sources for measuring and projecting the role of U.S. manufacturing in the global semiconductor manufacturing industry. We find that the government sources we consider face significant limitations for tracking semiconductor fab investment in real time: they use industry and product categories that are too broad, and come with substantial publication lags. We then analyze project-level alternative data from Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International (SEMI), which provides quarterly tracking of individual fab projects with greater timeliness and specificity. Comparing SEMI data with official statistics through 2023, we find broad consistency in investment levels, validating SEMI as a credible supplement to official statistics. This work provides both a practical guide for tracking real-time trends in semiconductor manufacturing and a case study in synthesizing government and alternative data sources.
title: Measuring and Projecting U.S. Investment in Semiconductor Manufacturing Capacity
